description: Hand-picked candidates that are not in the YC Summer 2026 RFS but are defensible as 'ahead of YC' — i.e. backed by signals that justify partner attention.

items.claim_summary: Personal RAG over a knowledge worker's full document trail (private; addresses the 'AI is plug-and-play' contradiction founders ship around)
items.rationale: YC RFS-007 covers 'personal RAG' but the contradiction-surfacing angle (vendor claims vs. integration reality) is not in the public RFS. Defensible as a wedge for tooling that targets the integration-pain proxy rather than the abstract retrieval problem.
signals: 5 founder interviews citing 6-month integration timelines vs. 'plug-and-play' claims
HN top post (2026-04) with 980 upvotes reporting the same gap
arXiv 2026.05678 — 'Browser-native context for personal retrieval' published 2026-04-27

items.claim_summary: Browser-native LLM agents with tab-level context — applying OS-level scheduler primitives to attention budgets
items.rationale: YC RFS-005 covers 'browser-native LLM agents' but does not call out the OS-scheduler analogy. Cross-domain transfer surfaces a structural pattern (scheduler → attention budget) that none of the public RFS items name.
signals: arXiv 2026.01234 design notes — explicit borrow from OS scheduler patterns
HN: 'Shipped a browser agent in 6 weeks' — 4 contradictions in the comments

items.claim_summary: Real-time data quality for AI training — borrow stream-processing fault-tolerance from finance ETL
items.rationale: YC RFS-003 covers training-data quality. The 'borrow from finance ETL' angle is a defensible specialization the public RFS does not name. Cross-domain pattern transfer.
signals: 5 training-pipeline post-mortems on arXiv (2026-Q1) all cite silent corruption
Finance industry blog posts on ETL fault tolerance (Jepsen-style)
